input.query: accidental breakage of glass windows doors coverage

output.answer:
Based on the RAA Contents PDS, coverage for accidental breakage of glass depends on what type of Insured Property is shown on your Certificate of Insurance:

**If Home is shown on your Certificate of Insurance:**
You are covered for the cost of repairing or replacing any part of any fixed glass forming part of the Insured Property, **including windows**, if accidentally broken. This also extends to fixed sinks or basins, shower bases (not tiled bases), baths, or toilets forming part of the Insured Property [RAA Contents PDS, page 52].

**If Contents is shown on your Certificate of Insurance:**
Coverage is limited to glass in furniture, pictures/paintings/prints/mirrors designed to be hung or freestanding, or glass forming part of aquariums, if accidentally broken [RAA Contents PDS, page 52]. This does not extend to fixed windows or doors of the Home itself — that coverage falls under the "Home" category above.

**Exclusions that apply regardless of category:**
This cover does **not** apply to:
- Repairing scratches (where the break does not extend through the entire thickness of the item)
- Glass in a glasshouse or greenhouse
- Repair or replacement of any tiles or tiled fixture or splashback (whether tiled or glass) forming part of the Home
- Toilet seats
- Glass forming part of a stove, heater, oven, or cook top as a result of the direct application of heat
- A picture tube or screen of a television or visual display unit
- Glass forming part of a radio or clock, vase, ornament, lamp, or photo frame
[RAA Contents PDS, page 52]

**Note on doors:** The excerpts specifically mention "windows" as an example of fixed glass covered under Home, but do not explicitly list "doors" or glass forming part of doors. I cannot confirm from the provided excerpts whether glass in doors is included, though it may fall under "fixed glass forming part of the Insured Property" if doors are considered part of the Insured Property structure. The excerpts do not provide enough detail to confirm this definitively — you may need to check additional PDS pages or your Certificate of Insurance for clarification.

This coverage is also subject to the General Exclusions found on pages 53–60, which are not fully detailed in the excerpts provided [RAA Contents PDS, page 52].
